messages:
maya: Thinking out loud — we need to pick an approach for collector topology for private clusters. Agent-only vs gateway-only vs hybrid. Main constraints: per-signal retention (spans/logs/metrics), per-tenant export limits, and minimizing cross-node egress. Thoughts?

liam: +1 to making it explicit. Agent-only is simplest for tenant isolation but increases number of exporters talking to SaaS endpoints (rate limits). Gateway centralizes exporters but is a single failure/egress point.

satoshi: We also need to consider resource variance on customer nodes. Agents can be very noisy (OOMs) if we run heavy processors. Gateway lets us size exporters in k8s.

olivia: For the console UX, customers will expect per-route retention controls (e.g., keep traces 7d vs 90d). Where do we enforce that? Agent-level config or gateway?

devon: My leaning: hybrid. Lightweight agent on host that does local batching + prefix/KV cache and forwards to a gateway in the VPC. Gateway handles heavy processors, sampling, export retries, and retention enforcement. That avoids per-node exporter sprawl.

maya: Hybrid sounds good but how do we represent pipelines per-signal? I don't want one giant pipeline that switches behavior based on signal type at runtime — testing matrix explodes.

liam: We can keep separate pipelines in the gateway collector config: one for traces, one for metrics, one for logs. Agent forwards to all three endpoints or to a single multiplexing endpoint on the gateway. Example proto route in OTEL config: 

```yaml
service: agent
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  batch: {}
exporters:
  otlp/gateway:
    endpoint: gateway:4317
service: 
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, probabilistic_sampler]
      exporters: [otlp/gateway]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/gateway]
```

satoshi: That matches what we've discussed before. Two operational notes: 1) probabilistic_sampler at gateway lets us reduce high-cardinality traces centrally; 2) retention enforcement needs a metadata store (per-tenant TTL) — stateless collector can't evict already-exported data.

olivia: Right — retention enforcement at gateway means exports to our long-term store include TTL metadata so the store can expire. For hosted mode we control storage; for private on-prem, we need to expose policy enforcement hooks so customers can opt in. UI needs toggle and clear text about where data is deleted.

devon: On quotas and routing: gateway should implement per-tenant token bucket and smart routing. If tenant exceeds export quota to an external exporter, gateway can fall back to: 1) buffer to disk (best-effort), 2) drop low-priority signals, or 3) route to a cheaper model/exporter. Would add config: `quota.action: buffer|drop|route`

maya: Any thoughts about agent -> gateway protocol? Plain OTLP (grpc) over mTLS is fine, but do we want a lightweight multiplexing protocol to reduce head-of-line blocking?

liam: OTLP/gRPC with keepalive + many streams should be fine. If we hit HoL we can enable multiple connections per agent. Also use the batch processor to reduce request rate.

satoshi: We should also plan for network partitions. Agent should have local disk queue + backpressure. Add a watchdog to limit disk usage per tenant. Otherwise tenant-level runaway will fill volumes.

olivia: UX question: in console when you configure retention do we show "agent-enforced" vs "gateway-enforced"? Some customers will want local retention for compliance (air-gapped) and others prefer central.

devon: Present both as options but default to gateway enforcement for hosted and dedicated. For private on-prem, default agent enforcement with a signed attest that shows deletion occurred (audit log).

maya: Operational concern: upgrades. Agents should be minimal so we can roll them without touching customers too much. Gateway can handle schema migrations and new processors.

liam: +1. Also we should version our pipeline configs, e.g., `pipelines.v2` with a compatibility layer in gateway collector. This allows gradual rollouts like `canary-pipeline` names.

collector-bot: Deploy job queued for `gateway/pipelines/v2` — staging cluster. CI pipeline: ./ci/deploy_gateway.sh --config pipelines/v2.yaml :rocket:

maya: Nice. Next steps: 1) write hybrid reference architecture doc, 2) draft OTEL config examples (agent + gateway), 3) spec retention metadata + export contract, 4) UX mock for retention/quotas. Volunteers?

liam: I'll take the OTEL examples.

satoshi: I'll draft the retention metadata + contract.

olivia: I'll do the UX mock and copy for legal on audit language.

devon: I'll put together the hybrid reference arch diagram and failure modes list.

maya: Great — created a GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/462 — add your PR refs there. Thanks all :thumbsup:
